facts_and_constraints: The long-wavelength absorption maxima are measured in two solvents for each identity.
Source-series NMR/IR ranges are contextual observations, not individual per-form measured reference spectra.
Only7a has the specific14.07ppm feature included here; it must not be treated as a measured feature of every molecule.

For the 7a proton resonance at 14.07 ppm, main PDF p14 labels the 1H NMR medium DMSO-d6 (500 MHz), whereas the SI PDF p155 spectrum acquisition panel labels SOLVENT CDCl3, TE 296.4 K and SFO1 500.1340010 MHz. Both sources show the same reported shift. The solvent provenance is unresolved; these annotations do not establish two independently measured solvent-specific observations. Do not select one label as definitive, infer solvent invariance, or treat either as an unambiguous quantitative calibration target without independent evidence.
identity_provenance: Main Scheme3 and source structural records define N-phenyl identities7a/8a/5g. The V1 source-connected drawings are retained without the Z label or exocyclic stereo; author form assignments and alternate candidate library are private.

out_of_scope: Restrict the investigation to the three supplied N-phenyl pyrazolone identities and their source solution optical observations. Preserve heavy-atom connectivity, total stoichiometry and explicit charge/state accounting in any derived representation. The supplied valence drawings are identity encodings and do not establish a unique solution species or configuration. Absorption in CHCl3/DMF, NMR in CDCl3/DMSO-d6 and solid-state IR have different environments; do not merge their conditions. The NH-pyrazolone series, antimicrobial assays, cell imaging and bulk fluorescence are outside the question. The 7a14.07ppm NMR solvent provenance is unresolved between main p14 and SI p155; preserve this limitation when using that datum.

limitations: Source computed evidence is not a calibrated error model for these solution spectra. Missing raw instrument errors, aggregate NMR/IR ranges and media differences limit quantitative identification. Expanded alternative-reference and V2 semantic calibration/isolation remain pending. The7a14.07ppm NMR solvent is source-ambiguous (main DMSO-d6; SI CDCl3); this limits solvent-specific interpretation without blocking the optical question.
